subject: Contract endgame: notice window and termination-for-convenience options
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@lawfirm.com>, legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed redlines: auto-renew + termination for convenience

Sean —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team reviewed the MSA + Order Form and asked us to propose a compromise on term/renewal/termination language before we go to procurement. Two quick asks from Acme:

1) Auto-renew: we want the Order Form to auto-renew annually unless Customer gives 60 days prior written notice.
2) Termination for convenience: add a Customer termination-for-convenience right with 60 days' notice and a termination fee equal to one (1) month of fees or pro-rata refund for prepaid months.

We attached a redline to show where we'd like the changes. Can you run this by your legal ops and let us know your preferred positions? We want to keep momentum this week — can you confirm a timeline for final redlines and a DocuSign-ready version?

Thanks,
Olivia Park
Head of Partnerships, Acme Health
olivia.park@acmehealth.com

Attachments: Acme_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx (redline), summary-termination-options.pdf (Acme asks)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 10:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Proposed redlines: auto-renew + termination for convenience

Forwarding Acme's redline. High level: they want 60-day auto-renew opt-out and a customer convenience termination with a 1-month fee. They asked for timeline this week.

My suggested positions to negotiate:
- Auto-renew: propose 90 days instead of 60 OR keep 60 but require written notice to both parties and include a reminder email 120 days out (gives ops time).
- Termination for convenience: don't accept a flat termination fee for hosted customers. Offer 60-day notice + pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts; for Dedicated (reserved capacity) carve out a 3-month minimum commitment and apply a 1-month cancellation charge if termination occurs within the initial commit window.

Attachments: I attached the customer's redline and a one-pager with our proposed language (Acme_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx). Can legal quickly sign off on the Dedicated carve? We need to push back on a universal termination fee — that will blow margins.

Next steps: Laura/Karthik, can you propose final MSA/OF language by EOD Friday? I will coordinate with Olivia for a quick call if needed.

—Sean
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 11:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed redlines: auto-renew + termination for convenience

Team —

Quick take from Legal Ops and Commercial:
- Auto-renew: we can accept Customer opt-out at 60 days if we add a mutual notice requirement and a reminder cadence (120/90/60 days) to reduce surprise churn. Include explicit statement that renewals are for the same term and pricing unless otherwise agreed.

- Termination for convenience: for Hosted/usage customers, we should not collect a flat termination fee. Instead offer 60-day notice + pro-rata refund for any prepaid fees and final invoice for usage through termination date. For Dedicated (Reserved Capacity) orders, accept a termination-for-convenience right only with the following: (a) minimum remaining commitment of 3 months or payment in lieu (customer pays remainder or a 1-month early termination charge, whichever is less), (b) 60-day notice. This preserves capacity economics.

- Language suggestions: include a defined "Termination Fee" only for Dedicated orders and explicitly exclude credits for operational work already performed (e.g., provisioning/setup costs) unless documented in SOW.

I added recommended redlines to the attached doc. Also: note HubSpot deal HS-45321 and aim to get a DocuSign-ready package by next Wednesday so sales can close this month.

Laura Bennett
VP, Legal & Business Affairs
Redwood Inference

Related: HS-45321, DocuSign draft link: https://www.docusign.com/starting/ABC123456789

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@acmehealth.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@lawfirm.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Proposed redlines: auto-renew + termination for convenience

Olivia / Maya —

Thanks for the redline. We reviewed internally and want to propose the following compromise so both teams can proceed quickly: 

1) Auto-renew: Auto-renew annually. Customer may opt out with 60 days' prior written notice, provided Redwood provides reminder notices at 120, 90 and 60 days. Renewal will be for the same term and pricing unless otherwise agreed in writing.

2) Termination for convenience (Customer): Customer may terminate for convenience with 60 days' written notice. For Hosted (pay-as-you-go) services, Redwood will provide a pro-rata refund of any prepaid fees for the remainder of the billing period. For Dedicated / Reserved Capacity orders, termination for convenience may be exercised but subject to a 3-month minimum remaining commitment; if termination occurs before that minimum, Customer will pay the lesser of (a) the remaining 3 months of committed fees, or (b) an early-termination charge equal to one month of fees. This protects our capacity planning and is intended to be narrowly scoped to Dedicated capacity only.

3) Operational carve-outs: We will not reimburse certain non-recurring setup costs unless specifically enumerated in the SOW.

I've attached a redline with the specific MSA/Order Form edits (Acme_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx). Please review and let us know if Acme can accept the Dedicated carve and the 60-day cadence. If Acme prefers a shorter notice window for commercial reasons, we can discuss early-termination charge trade-offs on the Dedicated side.

If this looks OK in principle, I'll produce a DocuSign-ready OF by Wednesday.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Acme_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@lawfirm.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Olivia Park <olivia.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines: auto-renew + termination for convenience

Sean —

Thanks for the detailed response and the redline. We discussed internally and Acme's position is: we can accept the Dedicated carve (3-month minimum) but would prefer a 45-day notice window rather than 60 days on both auto-renew opt-out and termination-for-convenience. Additionally, Acme requests an early-termination payment of 15% of the remaining committed fees (instead of the 1-month flat fee) if termination occurs within the initial 12 months of a Dedicated commitment. That gives them a smaller penalty but still recognizes sunk costs.

Please prepare a final redline reflecting: 45-day notice (both opt-out and termination), Dedicated 3-month minimum with 15% early-termination charge for terminations within year 1, and the Hosted pro-rata refund approach. We'll aim to review that final redline same day.

Maya Singh
Counsel for Acme Health
maya.singh@lawfirm.com

On behalf of Acme Health
